problem_trigger: A bounded P05 producer assignment released after the flow-control remediation did not materialize into an observable producer-ready Tier-2 candidate. Repeated controller reconciliation then held replacement production because the failure had not been durably checkpointed.
prior_design: DH0003 retained finish-before-start, a hard WIP cap, live-state reconciliation, explicit assignment contracts, and aging/toil triggers. Producer assignments could still exist only as controller intent without an independently observable producer-ready artifact or explicit terminal negative result.
hypothesis_rationale: Treating invisible/non-materialized assignments as flow failures and requiring observable producer-ready state or an explicit terminal negative result before replacement allocation should reduce silent work loss and prevent repeated reissuance of the same assignment.
exact_change: No authority, scheduler, governance, security, or verification boundary changes. D keeps new Tier-2 production paused, records the P05 non-materialization as a process failure, and requires the next released assignment to have a bounded scope, kill condition, and observable completion/negative-result state. Reissuing the same invisible assignment without new evidence is prohibited by the controller hold.
expected_benefit: Make assignment aging actionable without adding scheduler coordination.
Prevent repeated reissuance of invisible work.
Preserve finish-before-start while allowing a clean later release decision.
risks: Observable-state requirements can become bookkeeping if they exceed the value of the work.
Holding production can underutilize producer compute if the failure was transient.
A separate checkpoint artifact must be folded into the canonical append-oriented design history before it is treated as fully reconciled.
evaluation_window: Next 3-6 healthy controller windows after a future bounded Tier-2 release.
evaluation_criteria: Every released Tier-2 assignment reaches an observable producer-ready candidate or explicit terminal negative result within two healthy D cycles.
No duplicate reissuance occurs while an assignment outcome is unknown.
Recovery/bookkeeping remains below roughly half of controller capacity across three windows.
C/D WIP remains at or below two absent a documented higher-EV exception.

observed_outcomes.observation: Current live PR state contains only deferred PR #70; no P05 producer-ready candidate is visible.
The controller has held new Tier-2 production across multiple reconciliations rather than bypassing the mandatory design-memory gate.

The failure appears to be a flow-observability/process issue rather than evidence that P05 itself is low value; the next allocation decision should reassess P05 against read-only alternatives after reconciliation.

failures_side_effects: The P05 assignment consumed allocation intent without producing an observable candidate.
The overdue checkpoint prolonged zero active Tier-2 WIP.
Repeated reconciliation became process toil without new mission evidence.
lessons: An assignment is not progress until it yields an observable candidate or explicit negative result.
Do not reissue invisible work reflexively.
Keep the recovery mechanism simple and inside the existing controller state rather than adding scheduler or authority layers.
This checkpoint is staged separately and must be incorporated into agent/design_history.json before the mandatory design-history gate is considered fully cleared.
